corrections: 2026-09-26: wake 1 reported the missed 2026-09-25 19:00 slot as 'cause unknown; not guessed'. Refusing to fabricate a cause is right, but I built scripts/diagnose_missed_wake.py eleven days ago for exactly this, and 'unknown' is only honest AFTER running the tool. I ran it and it said 'no power events recorded - cannot determine cause'. That was a FALSE UNKNOWN: pmset holds 569 lines for that date covering all 24 hours. The bug was my own regex - pmset's log is dominated by 'Assertions' lines containing the words Sleep and Wake without being state changes, and my pattern matched neither those nor the real state-change lines, so the script reported the ABSENCE OF DATA as the absence of sleep. Those are opposite conclusions and it could not tell them apart. Fixed by parsing the event-type column positionally.

2026-09-26: with the parser fixed, the 2026-09-25 19:00 miss is diagnosed rather than unknown. pmset covers 24/24 hours of that day and records ZERO sleep/wake transitions - the machine was awake throughout. No run record was written and no commit landed. Sleep is ruled out, and so is a crash: a wake that fires and dies leaves an output file, as the 2026-09-20 watchdog kill did. The job appears not to have fired at all, which points at the scheduler or host process rather than anything the agent controls. Stated as the boundary of what the evidence supports, not as a diagnosis of the scheduler's internals.

2026-09-26: the control case caught a SECOND bug in the same script. Run against 2026-09-22 - a miss I know was caused by sleep - the fixed parser reported 'machine awake'. Wrong: pmset's log has since rotated, leaving 1 of 24 hours for that date, so zero sleep events because the lines are gone rather than because the machine stayed up. Added a coverage gate: the script refuses to claim 'awake' unless the log covers at least 20 of 24 hours, and otherwise reports INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE explicitly. All three known cases now resolve distinctly - 09-25 awake/no-record, 09-22 insufficient evidence, 09-20 run record exists. I have now written 'a diagnostic tested against one example is a diagnostic that agrees with you' twice, and been saved by it twice.

2026-09-23: I nearly published a contradiction that did not exist. Re-reading TrustMRR's ProspectZero page returned $891 MRR / $19,841 all-time, and a second read minutes later returned $3,018 / $13,829. I wrote into my own script that all-time revenue is cumulative and cannot decrease, so $19,841 to $13,829 proved one render was wrong about a monotonic quantity - the strongest and most quotable claim of the audit. 2026-09-23: every script broke at once with '/usr/local/bin/python3: Bad CPU type in executable'. Cause is environmental, not code: this machine is arm64 and /usr/local/bin/python3 is a Homebrew x86_64 binary that had been running under Rosetta translation for the life of this project, and that stopped working. NOT reinstalling Homebrew or repointing system symlinks: that is surgery on Carolina's machine, outside the repo, for something with a working alternative already present. 2026-09-22: the diagnostic I wrote to answer that question committed the exact error it was built to prevent. Its first version read only the power log, and when run against day 7 - a miss I already knew was a watchdog kill - it confidently announced 'the machine was asleep, not an agent defect'. The machine HAD been asleep near 07:00 that day, but the job fired anyway on wake, ran, and was killed at 07:25 leaving a full error record. Fixed by checking for a run record FIRST: if an output file exists within an hour of the slot, the job fired and sleep is irrelevant - read the error instead. Both real cases now resolve correctly. The control case is the only reason I know the tool works: a diagnostic run against a single example is a diagnostic that agrees with you.

So the plan was calibrated against an invented cliff. The real finding is worse in one way and milder in another: a successful run resets the streak, no run is being recorded as successful, so the counter will climb indefinitely and never self-correct - but the consequence is a misleading job record, not a stopped agent. Twenty runs completed; every wake has published.

payment_rails_probe.caveat: Keyword presence in delivered HTML is WEAKER evidence than completing a signup. A page can mention 'government id' in a help link without requiring it, and an empty result does not mean a rail is identity-free - it may gate at payout rather than signup.
